purpose: Offline recorded-data reference and engineering evaluation for Vyana. No trained model, prospective prediction, live sensor evidence, or automatic SOS integration is supplied.
platform_citation: Pollard, T., Moody, B. E., Lehman, L., Gow, B., Fernandes, C., Xie, C., Johnson, A., Mark, R. G., and Heldt, T. (2026). PhysioNet as a global platform for biomedical research. Nature Health 1, 792-795. https://doi.org/10.1038/s44360-026-00096-z .

datasets.name: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database
datasets.format: WFDB signals, headers and expert reference annotations
datasets.license: Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0
datasets.citation: Moody, G., and Mark, R. (2005). MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database (version 1.0.0). PhysioNet. https://doi.org/10.13026/C2F305 . Also cite Moody GB and Mark RG, The impact of the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology 20(3):45-50 (2001).
datasets.use: Reference ECG waveforms, beat annotations and rhythm-analysis evaluation.
datasets.limits: Recorded clinical data, not AD8232 validation. Recordings 201 and 202 are from the same subject; keep patients separate in any future evaluation.

datasets.name: BIDMC PPG and Respiration Dataset
datasets.format: Original CSV signals, numerics, breath annotations and fixed metadata
datasets.license: Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0; retain the supplied modification notice
datasets.citation: Pimentel, M., Johnson, A., Charlton, P., and Clifton, D. (2018). BIDMC PPG and Respiration Dataset (version 1.0.0). PhysioNet. https://doi.org/10.13026/C2208R . Also cite Pimentel et al., Towards a Robust Estimation of Respiratory Rate from Pulse Oximeters, IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering 64(8):1914-1923 (2017), https://doi.org/10.1109/TBME.2016.2613124 .
signals: Synchronized ECG, PPG and respiration at 125 Hz
Monitor numerics including HR and SpO2 at 1 Hz
datasets.use: Paired electrical/optical recordings for offline monitoring and data-pipeline evaluation.
datasets.limits: Hospital monitor data, not raw MAX30102 red/IR calibration data. Not labelled for heart-attack or cardiac-arrest prediction.

datasets.name: MIT-BIH Malignant Ventricular Ectopy Database
datasets.format: WFDB signals, headers and rhythm annotations
datasets.license: Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0
datasets.citation: Albrecht, P., Moody, G., and Mark, R. MIT-BIH Malignant Ventricular Ectopy Database (version 1.0.0). PhysioNet. https://doi.org/10.13026/C22P44 . Also cite Greenwald SD, Development and analysis of a ventricular fibrillation detector, MIT MS thesis (1986).
signals: ECG with annotated rhythm episodes, including VT and VF
datasets.use: Clearly labelled recorded abnormal-rhythm examples and reference annotation inspection.
datasets.limits: Rhythm annotations are not beat labels or future-arrest predictions. VFDB and the Sudden Cardiac Death Holter collection share recordings.

datasets.name: Sudden Cardiac Death Holter Database
datasets.reason_not_downloaded: Long recordings for a later research study; overlaps VFDB and has incomplete audited annotations. Not needed for the current monitoring demo.

datasets.name: PTB-XL
datasets.reason_not_downloaded: Approximately 3 GB of 12-lead ECG material. The current AD8232 supplies one lead; infarction labels do not provide prospective heart-attack prediction. Retained as an optional reference.
